assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editors convert one base pair to another without double-strand cleavage, by fusing a deaminase to a catalytically impaired Cas protein. This is a chemical idea executed simply, it is a genuine game-changer, and the consequences for research and for therapy are already visible. It is molecular chemistry applied to the genome, and the chemistry-prize claim is distinct from the 2020 CRISPR prize.
assessment.attribution: Liu's laboratory conceived and developed the cytosine and adenine base editors, with Komor and Gaudelli as lead trainees. Nishida and Kondo reported a parallel cytidine-deaminase fusion, so priority needs care, but the conceptual and broad engineering contribution is clearly Liu's. A single-laureate prize is defensible. Adding a second name would dilute a clear attribution.
assessment.maturity: Independent adoption is very broad, and base-editing therapies have reached clinical trials with first patient results. Recognition is timely, though long-term clinical safety is still being established.
uncertainties: Whether the committee prefers to pair this with prime editing (B011) or keep base editing alone.
Parallel work by Nishida and Kondo may be argued to share priority, and I cannot verify exact dates from the supplied text.
Clinical durability and off-target profiles remain open.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Induced degradation of target proteins by recruiting E3 ligases is a new pharmacological modality. It turns a binder into a catalytic eliminator of the protein and reaches targets that are hard to drug. The mechanistic discovery of how thalidomide-type molecular glues work through cereblon adds a second, simple and surprising chemical principle. The impact is already large in medicinal chemistry.
assessment.attribution: Credit is split among three groups. Crews and colleagues made the first PROTACs, Handa and Ito identified cereblon as the thalidomide target, and Ciulli made the structure-based VHL-recruiting designs that made PROTACs practical. Deshaies, Sakamoto, Kim, Gray and Ito are also credited, so priority is contested. I choose the three whose contributions I find most decisive, and the choice is not obviously unique.
assessment.maturity: The concept is well confirmed by many groups and by clinical-stage degraders. Approved drugs from this modality are still pending, so recognition could be seen as slightly early, but the chemistry is solid.
uncertainties: Allocation among Crews, Deshaies, Handa and Ciulli is unresolved.
Compound discovery: PROTACs and molecular glues may need different recognition.
No approved PROTAC drug yet, to my knowledge.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Palladium-catalysed C-N coupling is a simple, general way to make aryl amines, and it is used daily in pharmaceutical and materials synthesis. It has proved its consequences for decades. It is a strong example of a straightforward route that transformed practical synthesis.
assessment.attribution: Buchwald and Hartwig independently developed the general catalytic amination, with ligand design that made it broad. Kosugi's earlier tin-amide work is a precursor and has a priority claim that the committee would need to weigh. Two laureates give a clean configuration.
assessment.maturity: The method has been fully confirmed over about 30 years and is used at industrial scale. It is long mature, and the question is only whether the 2010 cross-coupling prize leaves room for it.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2010 palladium cross-coupling prize may weigh against it.
Weight to give Kosugi's precursor reaction.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Massively parallel sequencing by synthesis with reversible terminator nucleotides turned genome sequencing into a routine, cheap measurement. This is a game-changer for biology and medicine. The chemistry of fluorescent reversible terminators and single-molecule clustering is central to the invention.
assessment.attribution: Balasubramanian and Klenerman founded the Solexa approach, with the chemistry of the reversible terminators and the surface arrays. Rothberg and Mayer have claims for other parallel methods, in different chemistry, and the credit in the supplied list is a mixture of technologies. A two-person prize around sequencing by synthesis is the cleanest configuration.
assessment.maturity: The method has been fully validated for about two decades and is the dominant sequencing platform. It is mature and arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Whether a chemistry prize should single out sequencing by synthesis over other parallel sequencing methods.
The roles of the commercial developers and of the Solexa team beyond the two named are not resolved here.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Halide perovskite absorbers took solar cell efficiency from a few percent to over 25 percent in little more than a decade, with solution processing. This is a new type of material with real consequences. It resembles the kind of material class that I would call a game-changer.
assessment.attribution: Miyasaka reported the first perovskite-sensitised cell, Park made the first solid-state device with stable, higher efficiency, and Snaith showed the efficient meso-superstructured and planar devices. Grätzel, Seok and Kanatzidis also have major contributions. The selection of three is difficult and priority is partly disputed.
assessment.maturity: Efficiency is independently confirmed in many laboratories. Operational stability and lead toxicity are unresolved, so full maturity for a prize is debatable and recognition may be early.
uncertainties: Long-term stability and commercialisation are not demonstrated.
Allocation among Miyasaka, Park, Snaith, Grätzel, Seok and Kanatzidis is contested.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Energy landscape and funnel theory explains how proteins fold quickly despite a huge conformational space, and ties directly to experimental kinetics such as phi-value analysis. This is the quantitative theory-to-experiment link that I value. It is foundational for the way biomolecular simulation and structure prediction are understood.
assessment.attribution: Bryngelson and Wolynes first formulated the funnel concept, with Onuchic and Dill developing it, and Fersht made the experimental mapping of folding transition states. Five credited names exceed a prize, and the theory and experimental parts could be argued as a compound discovery. I choose a theory pair plus the experimental anchor.
assessment.maturity: The framework is well confirmed, though it is conceptual and its predictive power has partly been overtaken by the 2024 prize for structure prediction. Timeliness is uncertain.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2024 prize for protein design and structure prediction.
Priority between Bryngelson, Wolynes, Onuchic and Dill is disputed.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Descriptor-based theory, notably d-band and adsorption-energy scaling relations, lets one compute and design catalysts from first principles. It has been tested quantitatively against experiments on ammonia, hydrogen evolution and other reactions. It is a clear case of simple theory connected to measurement with practical consequences.
assessment.attribution: Nørskov is the leading originator of the computational descriptor approach in catalysis. Mavrikakis, Rossmeisl, Scheffler and Jaramillo contributed in important ways, but I find a single-laureate attribution fair. Some of the underlying d-band ideas stem from earlier work that is not credited in this list.
assessment.maturity: The concept is well confirmed and widely used in computational catalysis. Actual catalysts first found by computation are still few, so impact is partly methodological.
uncertainties: Earlier d-band and chemisorption theory by others, not in the list, may share priority.
Few catalysts fully predicted ab initio and then commercialised.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Reading nucleic-acid sequence by the ionic current through a single nanopore is simple in principle and has led to portable long-read sequencing. It is a new analytical measurement that is already widely used, including for field work.
assessment.attribution: Deamer, Branton and Kasianowicz proposed and first demonstrated polynucleotide translocation, Bayley engineered protein pores, and Akeson developed the enzyme ratcheting to control motion. Credit is spread over more than three people, and I cannot confirm every contribution from the supplied text. My three-name choice leaves out the pore-engineering contribution, which is a real weakness.
assessment.maturity: The method is validated and in routine use. Accuracy has improved steadily, and recognition would be timely, but it may be seen as technology more than a chemical discovery.
uncertainties: Whether to include Bayley's protein-pore engineering and Kasianowicz's early work.
Status of some credited individuals is not verified by me.
